TITLE: Evaluating Prior Speculative Decoding Attempts
PROPOSAL: Implement a systematic comparison of prior works that applied speculative decoding to VLMs, focusing on the draft model architectures, target model sizes, and multimodal datasets used. Include a qualitative analysis of each experiment's design choices and limitations.
CONTROLS: Compare baseline results from prior works (e.g., the 7B VLM draft model in the problem statement) against their own proposed modifications.
COST: Estimated 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to confirm the modest (1.5x) speedup reported in prior works and identify key limitations in their approaches, likely stemming from the shallow or poorly-designed draft models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Two-Stage Speculative Decoding for VLMs
PROPOSAL: Introduce a two-stage speculative decoding procedure for VLMs: (1) an image-encoder-based draft model processes the input image to generate high-level visual features, and (2) a text-generator draft model takes these features and the input text to propose candidate token sequences. The final output is then verified by the target VLM.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed two-stage approach against a single-stage approach using only a text-generator draft model (a common prior work method) and against an ablation where the image-encoder-based draft model is removed.
COST: Estimated 200 GPU-hours (requiring 4 V100 GPUs for 5 days)
PREDICTION: We expect to see a 2-3x speedup with moderate quality drop compared to ground truth outputs, and note that this two-stage approach may address the limitations of shallow draft models by leveraging complementary strengths from both the image-encoder and text-generator components.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Weighted-Average Draft Training for VQAVLMs
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel draft model training method, Weighted-Average Draft Training (WADT), for VVMs, particularly VQAVLMs. WADT uses a combination of two tasks: (i) predicting the target VLM's outputs on synthetic multimodal data, and (ii) evaluating the draft model's own output with minimal supervision. The two tasks are combined using a weighted average of the corresponding losses.
CONTROLS: Ablation experiment comparing WADT with standalone task i and task ii, as well as a baseline draft model trained on synthetic data using only task i; Also control for the value of the trainable weighing coefficients
COST: Estimated 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect WADT to result in better-performing draft models, reduced quality drop between the draft's proposals and the target model's output, and potentially enhanced robustness to diverse multimodal tasks.

PROPOSAL: Introduce an adaptive weighting scheme for WADT, where the relative importance of the two tasks and the additional pathway mechanism (APM) is dynamically adjusted based on the draft model's performance on a validation set.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Augmenting the Target VLM with Attention Distillation
PROPOSAL: Design an attention distillation module that extracts informative attention patterns from the target VLM and passes this information to the draft model, allowing it to better focus on relevant visual and textual input aspects.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed attention distillation module against a stand-alone attention-based draft model and against a target VLM trained with additional attention supervision.
COST: Estimated 250 GPU-hours (requiring additional computational resources for training the target VLM with attention supervision)
PREDICTION: We expect attention distillation to significantly improve the speedup and output quality of the speculative decoding workflow, highlighting the crucial role of attention in multimodal generative tasks.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: 4. Augmenting the Target VLM with Attention Distillation
PROPOSAL: Modify the attention distillation module to focus on the spatial attention patterns of the target VLM, rather than attempting to distill the entire attention matrix. This will allow the draft model to better capture the localized relationships between visual and textual features.
CONTROLS: Compare the revised attention distillation module against the original version, as well as against a baseline approach where the draft model is trained without attention distillation.
COST: Estimated 50 GPU-hours (requiring minimal additional computational resources)
PREDICTION: We expect the revised attention distillation module to demonstrate improved performance, particularly in tasks where localized attention is crucial, and to reduce the computational overhead associated with distilling the entire attention matrix.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Contextual Multi-Task Draft Model
PROPOSAL: Introduce a contextual multi-task draft model that jointly predicts multiple modalities (e.g., text, image, and audio) to better understand the contextual relationships between them. This can be achieved by incorporating multiple output heads for each modality and using a shared encoder to process the input.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed contextual multi-task draft model against a standalone multi-modal draft model, as well as against a baseline draft model that predicts only a single modality.
COST: Estimated 300 GPU-hours (requiring additional computational resources for training the contextual multi-task model)
PREDICTION: We expect the contextual multi-task draft model to demonstrate improved performance on tasks that require understanding complex contextual relationships between multiple modalities, and to offer a scalable solution for processing diverse multimodal inputs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning from Pretrained Language and Vision Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of transferring knowledge from large, pretrained language and vision models to the construction of a VLM draft model. We hypothesize that this transfer learning approach can help the draft model capture generic visual and textual features that are beneficial for various multimodal tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of draft models trained from scratch against those initialized with transferred knowledge from a large, pretrained language model (e.g., BERT) and/or a vision model (e.g., ViT).
COST: Estimated 20 GPU-hours (requiring minimal additional computational resources)
PREDICTION: We expect the transfer learning approach to yield improved draft model performance, particularly on tasks where recognizing generic visual and textual patterns is crucial, and to require fewer training epochs and data to achieve converged performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Deploying Speculative Decoding on a Real-World Multimodal Scenario
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the speculative decoding workflow on a real-world, diverse multimodal scenario, such as a chatbot conversing with users through a combination of text, images, and speech. This will demonstrate the practical feasibility and efficiency of our proposed methods in a real-world setting.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the speculative decoding workflow against a baseline approach that utilizes the target VLM without speculative decoding, and analyze the speedup achieved and the quality of the output.
COST: Estimated 1,000 GPU-hours (requiring significant computational resources for the deployment and evaluation of the multimodal scenario)
PREDICTION: We expect the speculative decoding workflow to demonstrate significant efficiency gains and high-quality output in the real-world multimodal scenario, showcasing the potential for practical deployment and further development in real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models using Hugging Face's CLIP
PROPOSAL: Implement and evaluate a version of speculative decoding on VLMs using a VLM-specific draft model, where the draft model incorporates the CLIP image encoder and a small companion language model, fine-tuned on image captioning tasks with a goal of improved accuracy and speedup relative to prior work.
CONTROLS: Implement identical counterparts with naive (i.e., computing the full autoregressive sequence) and weak draft models with either a pre-trained but less accurate image encoder (e.g. DALL-E) or no image encoder at all.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected speedups of 1.8-2.2x on 7B VLMs, but potentially lower than the text-only case due to image encoding overhead; we may need image encoder optimizations to realize higher speedups.

(Research question 1 addressed: how to effectively apply speculative decoding to VLMs.)

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Extending Speculative Decoding to Visual Question Answering via Training with Adversarial Image Perturbations
PROPOSAL: Modify the training procedure for the VLM draft model to include adversarial image perturbations, aimed at improving its robustness against small image variations. Train the draft model with a mix of original images and adversarial images (e.g., created using the PGD method), with the goal of enhancing its ability to attend to the most relevant visual features in challenging scenarios, such as visual question answering.
CONTROLS: Compare with a version of the draft model trained without these perturbations, and with a conventional supervised learning baseline.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Improved accuracy and robustness on visual question answering tasks, with a potential reduction in mean average precision (mAP) error by 5-10%.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models using Hugging Face's CLIP | Extending Speculative Decoding to Vision-Language Models via Additional Dense Interaction Layers
PROPOSAL: Introduce additional dense interaction layers between the VLM draft model and the image encoder, to better capture and prune the most relevant visual information. The layers will be designed to extract higher-level features from the input images, which can be used to inform the draft model's textual predictions.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original version of speculative decoding, as well as a variant without these additional interaction layers.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected speedups of 2.0-2.4x on 7B VLMs, improved accuracy on image captioning and visual question answering tasks, and better robustness to image variations.

(This revision consolidates the ideas of existing proposals, making them more efficient and easier to implement, while still addressing the research questions.)

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models using Hugging Face's CLIP | Efficient Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models using Hugging Face's CLIP with Progressive Merge
PROPOSAL: Modify the draft model to use a progressive merge strategy, where it iteratively adds image embeddings to the input sequence in a hierarchical manner, with the most important visual features being added first. This allows the draft model to focus on the most relevant image information and reduce computational overhead.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original version of speculative decoding, as well as a variant without progressive merge.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected speedups of 2.1-2.5x on 7B VLMs, improved accuracy on image captioning and visual question answering tasks, and better robustness to image variations.

(This revised proposal addresses the limitations of the original idea and is expected to yield better results.)

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Creating the Necessary Multimodal Dataset for Training Robust Draft Models
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive dataset that pairs large, diverse collections of images with extended assistant responses, focusing on tasks like visual question answering, image captioning, and video question answering. This dataset can be used to fine-tune a VLM draft model to generate high-quality candidate responses that are suitable for speculative decoding.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the draft model's performance on various benchmarks, comparing it to other state-of-the-art VLMs.
COST: 500 GPU-hours (dataset creation) + 100 GPU-hours (model fine-tuning and testing)
PREDICTION: High-quality candidate responses will significantly improve speculative decoding efficiency, leading to speedups above 2.5x on 7B VLMs.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE:  Extending Speculative Decoding to Visual Question Answering via Training with Adversarial Image Perturbations | Semantic Aware Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: Introduce a semantic-aware module to the draft model, which utilizes the generated textual candidate responses to compute a relevance score for each image feature. This score is then used to selectively add or remove visual features to improve the draft model's performance on visual question answering tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare with the original version of speculative decoding for visual question answering, as well as a baseline that uses the original draft model without the semantic-aware module.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected accuracy improvements of 10-15% on visual question answering benchmarks, and significant robustness gains against adversarial inputs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Transfer Learning of Encoder Parameters from High-Resource Visual Tasks to Vision-Language Modeling
PROPOSAL: Explore the potential benefits of fine-tuning the VLM's image encoder on high-resource tasks (e.g., image classification, object detection) before using it for speculative decoding. This could enable the encoder to learn strong representations for images that transfer well to vision-language tasks.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the VLM with encoder parameters fine-tuned on high-resource tasks, compared to the standard training procedure.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Achievable 5-10% improvements in image captioning and visual question answering tasks, due to the pre-trained encoder's ability to learn robust and generalizable visual features.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE:  Creating the Necessary Multimodal Dataset for Training Robust Draft Models | Automated Dataset Augmentation via Deep Generative Models
PROPOSAL: Utilize deep generative models (e.g., VQ-VAE, Flow) to automatically augment the multimodal dataset created in the previous proposal. The generated samples can be used to enrich the diversity and quantity of the original dataset, potentially leading to more robust and generalizable draft models.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the data augmentation strategy's effectiveness by comparing results obtained with the augmented dataset to those obtained with the original dataset.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Achievable 5-10% improvement in accuracy on image captioning and visual question answering tasks, resulting from the larger, more diverse dataset, and better-trained draft models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Minimizing Inference Time and Memory Overheads of Speculative Decoding on Vision-Language Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate techniques to optimize the inference time and memory overheads of speculative decoding on VLMs. This could include pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation, which may be essential to achieving higher speedups and accelerating the widespread adoption of speculative decoding for VLMs.
CONTROLS: Compare the optimized version with non-optimized version of speculative decoding, and evaluate the effect on inference time and memory usage.
COST: 160 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Achievable 20-30% reduction in inference time, and a corresponding reduction in memory overhead, depending on the specific optimization techniques applied.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Minimizing Inference Time and Memory Overheads of Speculative Decoding on Vision-Language Models | Efficient Approximation of Image Embeddings using Learned Hashing
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of learned hashing techniques to compactly represent image embeddings, reducing the memory overhead of speculative decoding on VLMs. This could involve training a separate hashing model to produce a fixed-size hash code for each image embedding, which can then be used to accelerate inference.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of speculative decoding with the compact image embedding representation to the original speculative decoding framework, focusing on latency, accuracy, and memory overhead.
COST: 140 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Achievable 5-15% reduction in inference time, and a corresponding reduction in memory overhead, depending on the specific hashing technique applied. This efficient approximation could make speculative decoding even more practical for large-scale VLM deployments.
